question: A senior operator is building an energy baseline for one pressure zone before any pump changes are funded. Which set of inputs must be captured together for that baseline to mean anything?
correctAnswer: Metered flow, discharge head, and electricity use recorded over the same time period
explanation: A baseline is only comparable when flow, head, and electricity use describe the same operating period, so later changes can be judged against it.
options: Motor nameplate ratings, pump ages, and the original purchase price of each unit
Metered flow, discharge head, and electricity use recorded over the same time period
Operator shift notes, valve counts, and the number of hydrants in the pressure zone
Daily rainfall totals, road salt records, and customer calls about taste and odour
optionA: Motor nameplate ratings, pump ages, and the original purchase price of each unit
optionB: Metered flow, discharge head, and electricity use recorded over the same time period
optionC: Operator shift notes, valve counts, and the number of hydrants in the pressure zone
optionD: Daily rainfall totals, road salt records, and customer calls about taste and odour
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy strategy for pumping. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Support Systems: Energy strategy for pumping

question: A utility is opening a new ten year capital forecast cycle. Which set of inputs belongs at the start of that forecast, before projects are priced?
correctAnswer: Asset condition, remaining service life, growth demand, and the service levels to be delivered
explanation: Forecasting starts from condition, remaining life, growth, and service levels; pricing and scheduling come after those needs are known.
options: Contractor bid tabs, paving schedules, and the dates of the next three council elections
Last year invoices, overtime totals, and the number of vehicles assigned to each crew
Asset condition, remaining service life, growth demand, and the service levels to be delivered
Chemical delivery records, hydrant paint colours, and the age of the office computer fleet
optionA: Contractor bid tabs, paving schedules, and the dates of the next three council elections
optionB: Last year invoices, overtime totals, and the number of vehicles assigned to each crew
optionC: Asset condition, remaining service life, growth demand, and the service levels to be delivered
optionD: Chemical delivery records, hydrant paint colours, and the age of the office computer fleet
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Capital planning leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which zone profile makes a neighbourhood a strong candidate for a booster disinfection station?
correctAnswer: Long travel time from treatment, warm summer water, and residuals that fade before reaching customers
explanation: Booster stations earn their place where travel time and warm water pull residuals down before the water reaches customers.
options: Long travel time from treatment, warm summer water, and residuals that fade before reaching customers
Short travel time from treatment, cold winter water, and residuals that stay high at every tap
A new subdivision beside the plant, oversized new mains, and no history of residual complaints
A zone fed by gravity alone, with no storage, no dead ends, and steady demand through the year
optionA: Long travel time from treatment, warm summer water, and residuals that fade before reaching customers
optionB: Short travel time from treatment, cold winter water, and residuals that stay high at every tap
optionC: A new subdivision beside the plant, oversized new mains, and no history of residual complaints
optionD: A zone fed by gravity alone, with no storage, no dead ends, and steady demand through the year
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Booster disinfection programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Before any incident happens, which element must a utility emergency plan settle in writing?
correctAnswer: Who holds authority to make operating decisions, notify agencies, and speak for the utility
explanation: Preassigned decision, notification, and communication authority prevents delay and conflicting direction when an incident begins.
options: Which staff members will volunteer to work unpaid hours during the first day of an event
Which radio station will carry interviews once the incident has been fully resolved
Which supplier will offer the lowest price for bottled water during a future shortage
Who holds authority to make operating decisions, notify agencies, and speak for the utility
optionA: Which staff members will volunteer to work unpaid hours during the first day of an event
optionB: Which radio station will carry interviews once the incident has been fully resolved
optionC: Which supplier will offer the lowest price for bottled water during a future shortage
optionD: Who holds authority to make operating decisions, notify agencies, and speak for the utility
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Emergency leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which record keeping habit best keeps a distribution utility ready for a provincial inspection at any time?
correctAnswer: Keeping sampling, maintenance, and corrective action records current, complete, and easy to retrieve
explanation: Readiness is a year round condition: complete, current, retrievable records show how the system is actually being run.
options: Rebuilding the full record set from memory in the week before an inspector is expected to arrive
Storing records with individual operators so each person can describe only their own work
Keeping sampling, maintenance, and corrective action records current, complete, and easy to retrieve
Keeping only the records for the current month and discarding older files to reduce clutter
optionA: Rebuilding the full record set from memory in the week before an inspector is expected to arrive
optionB: Storing records with individual operators so each person can describe only their own work
optionC: Keeping sampling, maintenance, and corrective action records current, complete, and easy to retrieve
optionD: Keeping only the records for the current month and discarding older files to reduce clutter
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Inspection readiness leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A crew is setting up unidirectional flushing on a problem segment. Which sequence describes that method correctly?
correctAnswer: Isolate the segment, then move water from a clean source outward along one path at a planned velocity
explanation: Unidirectional flushing works because an isolated segment is scoured along a single controlled path at a velocity high enough to lift deposits.
options: Isolate the segment, then move water from a clean source outward along one path at a planned velocity
Open hydrants at random across the zone until the discharged water looks clear at each one
Push water back and forth through the segment by reversing the flow every few minutes
Close the whole zone, drain every main at once, and refill the network from the nearest tank
optionA: Isolate the segment, then move water from a clean source outward along one path at a planned velocity
optionB: Open hydrants at random across the zone until the discharged water looks clear at each one
optionC: Push water back and forth through the segment by reversing the flow every few minutes
optionD: Close the whole zone, drain every main at once, and refill the network from the nearest tank
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Flushing and turnover programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A manager taking over a fleet of reservoirs across several zones needs one data set per facility. Which set supports fleet level decisions?
correctAnswer: Age, condition, usable capacity, turnover, inspection history, and remaining service life
explanation: Fleet decisions compare condition, capacity, turnover, inspection history, and remaining life across facilities, not site trivia.
options: Paint colour, fence style, ladder type, and the brand of lock fitted at each site gate
Crew lunch locations, snow clearing routes, and the distance to the nearest hardware store
Original construction contractor, ribbon cutting date, and the names of past operators
Age, condition, usable capacity, turnover, inspection history, and remaining service life
optionA: Paint colour, fence style, ladder type, and the brand of lock fitted at each site gate
optionB: Crew lunch locations, snow clearing routes, and the distance to the nearest hardware store
optionC: Original construction contractor, ribbon cutting date, and the names of past operators
optionD: Age, condition, usable capacity, turnover, inspection history, and remaining service life

question: An Overall Responsible Operator delegates daily operating duties to certified operators on shift. What remains with the ORO after that delegation?
correctAnswer: Accountability for ensuring qualified operators direct operations and required duties are carried out
explanation: Delegation assigns the work, but the ORO stays accountable for making sure qualified people direct operations and duties are done.
options: No further involvement, because delegation transfers all accountability to the shift operators
Accountability for ensuring qualified operators direct operations and required duties are carried out
Only the paperwork duties, because operating accountability moves to the municipal council
Responsibility for approving vacation schedules, with technical decisions left to suppliers
optionA: No further involvement, because delegation transfers all accountability to the shift operators
optionB: Accountability for ensuring qualified operators direct operations and required duties are carried out
optionC: Only the paperwork duties, because operating accountability moves to the municipal council
optionD: Responsibility for approving vacation schedules, with technical decisions left to suppliers

question: Electricity prices are lowest overnight and highest during the morning peak, and the zone has an elevated tank. Which scheduling decision cuts energy cost while pumping the same total volume?
correctAnswer: Fill the elevated tank overnight and let stored water supply more of the morning peak demand
explanation: Storage lets the utility shift pumping into low price hours and meet the peak from the tank instead of from peak price electricity.
options: Fill the elevated tank overnight and let stored water supply more of the morning peak demand
Run every booster pump together through the highest priced afternoon demand period each day
Keep the elevated tank nearly empty so the pumps respond directly to every demand change
Throttle the pump discharge valves during overnight filling to stretch the pumping window
optionA: Fill the elevated tank overnight and let stored water supply more of the morning peak demand
optionB: Run every booster pump together through the highest priced afternoon demand period each day
optionC: Keep the elevated tank nearly empty so the pumps respond directly to every demand change
optionD: Throttle the pump discharge valves during overnight filling to stretch the pumping window
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Energy strategy for pumping. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Break records cluster on one older trunk main, but a newer main in another ward has louder political support for replacement. Which ranking approach should leadership use for the renewal budget?
correctAnswer: Rank by likelihood and consequence of failure combined with cost, so the highest risk assets move first
explanation: Risk based ranking weighs how likely failure is and what it would cost the community, which age or visibility alone cannot show.
options: Rank by the age of each pipe alone, because the oldest asset is automatically the riskiest asset
Rank by the volume of complaints from each ward, because visibility is the fairest test available
Rank by which project is easiest to tender, because construction convenience protects the budget
Rank by likelihood and consequence of failure combined with cost, so the highest risk assets move first
optionA: Rank by the age of each pipe alone, because the oldest asset is automatically the riskiest asset
optionB: Rank by the volume of complaints from each ward, because visibility is the fairest test available
optionC: Rank by which project is easiest to tender, because construction convenience protects the budget
optionD: Rank by likelihood and consequence of failure combined with cost, so the highest risk assets move first
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Capital planning leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A booster station is verified to be feeding the set dose, yet residuals at the far end of the zone keep missing the program target. Which set of factors should the program review examine next?
correctAnswer: Water age, demand patterns, and mixing in the storage facility between the station and the sample point
explanation: When the dose leaving the station is right, residual loss usually sits downstream in water age, demand patterns, or storage mixing.
options: The colour of the station building, the age of the delivery truck, and the brand of sample bottles
Water age, demand patterns, and mixing in the storage facility between the station and the sample point
The number of fire hydrants painted this year and the schedule for mowing grass at the station
The chlorine supplier invoice total and the date the last chemical tote was delivered to the site
optionA: The colour of the station building, the age of the delivery truck, and the brand of sample bottles
optionB: Water age, demand patterns, and mixing in the storage facility between the station and the sample point
optionC: The number of fire hydrants painted this year and the schedule for mowing grass at the station
optionD: The chlorine supplier invoice total and the date the last chemical tote was delivered to the site
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Booster disinfection programs. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A trunk main break threatens to drain the zone that serves a hospital. Which set of actions should leadership drive in the first operating period?
correctAnswer: Confirm the isolation, protect pressure for critical users, and notify the affected critical customers directly
explanation: Protecting pressure for critical users and telling them directly what is happening comes before full repair planning in a major break.
options: Wait for a full damage estimate before isolating anything, so the repair plan can be priced first
Open every interzone valve at once so water can move freely, whatever the pressure effects may be
Confirm the isolation, protect pressure for critical users, and notify the affected critical customers directly
Send all available crews to the break site and leave customer notification until repairs are finished
optionA: Wait for a full damage estimate before isolating anything, so the repair plan can be priced first
optionB: Open every interzone valve at once so water can move freely, whatever the pressure effects may be
optionC: Confirm the isolation, protect pressure for critical users, and notify the affected critical customers directly
optionD: Send all available crews to the break site and leave customer notification until repairs are finished

options: Ask the crews to remember the missing dates and fill them in from memory at the next shift
Remove valve exercising from the maintenance program so the record gap stops appearing
Wait for a real inspector to raise the point before spending any time on the record system

question: Sediment complaints return every spring on a dead end main that sat at low demand all winter. Which program response fits that pattern?
correctAnswer: Schedule targeted flushing of the segment, record what the discharged water shows, and track repeat complaints
explanation: Targeted flushing removes the accumulated sediment, and recording results plus complaint trends shows whether the fix held.
options: Raise the disinfectant dose for the whole city until the complaints from that one street stop
Schedule targeted flushing of the segment, record what the discharged water shows, and track repeat complaints
Replace the service lines on the street, because sediment in the main cannot be removed by flushing
Tell residents the discolouration is seasonal and take no field action unless a main break occurs
optionA: Raise the disinfectant dose for the whole city until the complaints from that one street stop
optionB: Schedule targeted flushing of the segment, record what the discharged water shows, and track repeat complaints

question: The largest reservoir in a zone is booked out of service for cleaning during a warm spell. Which items must leadership confirm before the outage starts?
correctAnswer: Remaining storage, fire protection needs, pump capacity, and a refill plan covering the outage window
explanation: An outage is only safe once remaining storage, fire needs, pumping capacity, and refill timing are proven to cover the zone.
options: That the cleaning contractor has the newest pressure washer and a full crew available on weekends
That the reservoir roof can be repainted at the same time to save a second site visit later on
Remaining storage, fire protection needs, pump capacity, and a refill plan covering the outage window
That neighbouring zones can be told about the outage after the reservoir is already drained

optionC: Remaining storage, fire protection needs, pump capacity, and a refill plan covering the outage window

question: An ORO approves a planned reservoir outage that falls during the ORO vacation period. Which arrangement must be in place before the ORO leaves?
correctAnswer: A qualified acting ORO is named, briefed on the outage risks, and confirmed reachable at all times
explanation: Coverage only works when a qualified acting ORO is named, briefed on the specific risks, and reachable for the whole period.
options: A qualified acting ORO is named, briefed on the outage risks, and confirmed reachable at all times
The outage paperwork is filed with the municipality, and the shift operators are told to improvise
A junior operator is given the ORO phone, with instructions to call the ORO back from vacation
The reservoir outage is kept off the operating schedule so no one outside the crew knows of it

optionC: A junior operator is given the ORO phone, with instructions to call the ORO back from vacation

question: One station shows energy use per cubic metre up sharply over a season while its flow and discharge pressure hold steady. Which first action targets the likely cause?
correctAnswer: Inspect the pump for impeller wear, internal recirculation, and running away from its best efficiency point
explanation: Rising specific energy at steady flow and head points inside the pump: wear, recirculation, or operation off its best efficiency point.
options: Raise the discharge pressure setpoint so the pump works harder against the system curve each day
Inspect the pump for impeller wear, internal recirculation, and running away from its best efficiency point
Replace the electricity meter on the assumption that the pump condition will correct itself
Move the station to continuous full speed running and recheck the trend in the next budget year
optionA: Raise the discharge pressure setpoint so the pump works harder against the system curve each day
optionB: Inspect the pump for impeller wear, internal recirculation, and running away from its best efficiency point
optionC: Replace the electricity meter on the assumption that the pump condition will correct itself
optionD: Move the station to continuous full speed running and recheck the trend in the next budget year

question: Council asks leadership to defer a reservoir recoating project by five years to balance this year budget. Which information should leadership put in front of council with that request?
correctAnswer: The added deterioration risk, the likely higher future cost, and the service and quality effects of waiting

An assurance that five more years of coating failure will have no effect on the reservoir at all
The added deterioration risk, the likely higher future cost, and the service and quality effects of waiting
A list of unrelated projects in other departments that could also be deferred in the same year

optionB: An assurance that five more years of coating failure will have no effect on the reservoir at all
optionC: The added deterioration risk, the likely higher future cost, and the service and quality effects of waiting

question: Leadership is choosing a disinfectant product for a multi station booster program. Which set of factors should drive that choice?
correctAnswer: Residual stability, byproduct formation, storage and handling safety, feed reliability, and total program cost
explanation: Product choice at program scale balances residual performance, byproducts, safety, feed reliability, and whole program cost together.
options: Residual stability, byproduct formation, storage and handling safety, feed reliability, and total program cost
The colour of the delivery tote, the familiarity of the brand name, and the size of the product brochure
The distance from the supplier warehouse to the head office and the day of the week deliveries arrive
The preference of one operator, provided the product is the cheapest option per container this year

question: An inspector arrives unannounced while crews are mid repair on a broken watermain. Which response best serves both the repair and the inspection?
correctAnswer: Provide records and access as requested, keep the repair properly supervised, and explain any site constraints
explanation: Cooperation and candour during an unannounced visit, without abandoning supervision of live work, is what readiness looks like in practice.
options: Ask the inspector to return next month, because unannounced visits are not fair during repair work
Pull every operator off the repair to attend the inspector, leaving the excavation unsupervised
Provide records and access as requested, keep the repair properly supervised, and explain any site constraints
Limit the inspector to the office parking lot until the repair crew has fully restored the road

question: A storage tank keeps missing its turnover goal because level controls hold it near full all day. Which operating change addresses that cause?
correctAnswer: Widen the operating level band so a larger share of the stored volume exchanges with fresh water each day
explanation: Turnover improves when the level band lets a meaningful share of stored water leave and be replaced daily.
options: Widen the operating level band so a larger share of the stored volume exchanges with fresh water each day
Raise the high level setpoint further so the tank stays completely full through every demand cycle
Lower the disinfectant target for the zone so the older water in the tank passes its samples
Close the tank inlet at night and let the zone run on pumps alone until the morning peak ends

optionB: Raise the high level setpoint further so the tank stays completely full through every demand cycle
optionC: Lower the disinfectant target for the zone so the older water in the tank passes its samples

question: An operator reports discoloured water and a possible contamination concern in one zone late at night. Which ORO duty governs the next steps?
correctAnswer: Ensure the concern is assessed promptly, protective actions begin, and required notifications are made without delay

Ask the operator to keep the report informal until a second complaint arrives from the same street
Direct the operator to raise the chlorine dose and record nothing until the water clears again

question: One of two identical pumps runs on a variable speed drive while the other is throttled at fixed speed. Which evidence best supports converting the second pump as well?
correctAnswer: Measured energy per cubic metre and hours run at part load for each pump across a full season
explanation: A conversion case rests on measured specific energy and real part load hours over a season, not nameplates or spot readings.
options: Measured energy per cubic metre and hours run at part load for each pump across a full season
The nameplate horsepower of each motor, because identical ratings prove identical energy use
The opinion of the pump supplier, provided the drive can be delivered before the fiscal year end
A single afternoon of readings taken while both pumps happened to run at full speed together

question: During a pressure drop, a booster station chemical feed line is found connected so chemical could be drawn back toward the potable line. Which immediate decision is correct?

Raise the feed rate so positive chemical pressure overcomes any suction from the water line
Note the finding for the next annual program review and keep the station in normal operation

question: Water conservation pressure is rising, but a flushing program still has to clean problem segments properly. Which redesign holds both goals together?
correctAnswer: Set velocity and discharged water clarity endpoints by segment, so crews flush enough to clean and stop once clear
explanation: Segment specific endpoints clean the pipe and end the flush when the water runs clear, which is where conservation is honestly won.
options: Flush every segment for the same fixed time, because equal minutes are simpler to schedule and defend
Set velocity and discharged water clarity endpoints by segment, so crews flush enough to clean and stop once clear
Cut the flushing velocity in half across the city so the program uses less water on every segment
Stop flushing problem segments entirely and rely on customer complaints to identify dirty mains

optionB: Set velocity and discharged water clarity endpoints by segment, so crews flush enough to clean and stop once clear

question: A board questions why an aging booster station with repeated feed failures should not simply stay in service another five years. Which ORO response is defensible?

correctAnswer: 1.09 kg/day

question: A booster program holds 540 kg of disinfectant in stock. Station 1 uses 3600 m3/day boosted by 0.5 mg/L, using mass in grams equals volume in m3 times dose in mg/L and 1000 g equals 1 kg.
